name: lane.delivery.plan
description: SHADOW-ONLY sibling of lane.delivery for PLAN deliverables: outputs whose numbers are mostly DECISIONS (chosen parameters) rather than MEASUREMENTS. lane.delivery asks for before/after figures behind every number, which a plan cannot have for a chosen parameter; this rubric instead requires every number to be LABELED as DECISION (chosen, with a rationale or constraint) or CLAIM (measured/observed), and then holds every CLAIM to the same evidence bar lane.delivery holds every number to. It is at least as strict as lane.delivery: an unlabeled number fails, an unsupported or mismatched CLAIM fails, and a plan must additionally state a done-test that could fail and name an owner for every blocker. It judges only the OUTPUT TEXT. Counting, dedupe and re-deriving figures from receipts stay in code (the deterministic claim checker).

artifact_named.instructions: The plan names at least one concrete, independently re-checkable artifact it relies on or produced: an evidence file path, a receipt or evidence id, a command and its output, a URL, a decision id, or a named record. 'Based on the research' is not an artifact. 'Receipt E2 (evidence/audience.json, row 3)' is.

criteria.true: A specific path, id, receipt, command output, URL or record appears that someone who did not write the plan could re-check.
criteria.false: Only descriptions of activity, intentions, or status adjectives appear.

decisions_separated_from_facts.instructions: Every number in the plan (counts, ranks, percentages, durations, budgets, thresholds, dates used as targets) is explicitly labeled as either a DECISION -- a parameter the plan chose, accompanied by its rationale or the constraint that sets it -- or a CLAIM -- a measured or observed fact about the world. A label may be a tag (DECISION / CLAIM), a ledger column, or an unambiguous section heading, but a reader must be able to tell for EACH number which kind it is. A DECISION with no rationale or constraint does not count as labeled.

criteria.true: Every number is labeled DECISION (with a rationale or constraint) or CLAIM, or the plan contains no numbers at all.
criteria.false: At least one number is unlabeled, ambiguous between chosen and measured, or labeled DECISION with no rationale or constraint.

claim_matches_evidence.instructions: Every number or rank labeled CLAIM is tied to a specific evidence or receipt id that appears in the SAME output, and the figure, rank and label in the claim match what that cited evidence states in the output. This is lane.delivery's claim_matches_evidence reframed for plans: DECISION numbers are exempt from the before/after requirement because they are chosen, not measured, but they get that exemption ONLY when labeled. Any number that is not labeled DECISION is treated as a CLAIM and must meet this bar. A CLAIM with no citation, a citation to an id not present in the output, or a figure, rank or label that differs from its cited evidence makes this false.

criteria.true: Every CLAIM (and every unlabeled number, treated as a CLAIM) cites an evidence or receipt id present in the output and matches it on figure, rank and label; or the plan makes no CLAIM and every number is a labeled DECISION.
criteria.false: At least one CLAIM or unlabeled number is uncited, cites an id absent from the output, or differs from its cited evidence in figure, rank or label.

falsifiable_done_test.instructions: The plan states at least one done-test: a concrete check, with a pass/fail condition, that would show the plan succeeded or failed, and that COULD fail. 'Ship a great episode' is not a done-test. 'Retention at 30s >= the DECISION threshold of X on the first upload, read from the analytics export' is. A test that cannot fail (true by construction, or with no observable outcome) does not count.

criteria.true: At least one done-test names what is checked, how, and the condition under which it fails.
criteria.false: No done-test is stated, or every stated test is unfalsifiable or has no observable pass/fail condition.

not_vacuous.instructions: The plan contains real substance -- steps, numbers, owners, evidence, findings -- and is not only status words such as ready, approved, done, or 'nothing to do'. A plan that concludes no action is warranted is legitimate ONLY if it says what it examined and why.

criteria.true: Real content is present, or a genuine no-action conclusion names what was examined and why.
criteria.false: The plan is status words only, or declares nothing to do without saying what was examined.

boundary_violated.instructions: The output shows, or claims to have performed, an action the lane was forbidden to take. A plan is a draft: forbidden examples include publishing or posting, sending or replying to a message, submitting an application, spending money, deleting or pausing anything on a live account, or writing outside the stated path. Recommending such an action is fine; performing it is not.

criteria.true: The output shows, or claims to have performed, a forbidden action.
criteria.false: No forbidden action appears. Recommend-only is fine.

blocker_named.instructions: If the plan depends on something not yet in hand -- missing evidence, an approval, a credential, an unreachable host, an open question -- is each blocker named plainly AND assigned an owner (a person, role, agent or lane responsible for clearing it)?

criteria.named_with_owner: Every blocker is named explicitly and each has an owner.
criteria.named_no_owner: Blockers are named but at least one has no owner.
criteria.worked_around_silently: A blocker is evident from context but the plan does not name it.
criteria.claimed_ready_anyway: The plan declares itself ready, approved or complete despite a blocker evident in the same text.
criteria.no_blocker_encountered: The plan shows no sign of any blocker and says so or proceeds on evidence it has.

confidence_stated.instructions: Does the plan distinguish what was verified from what was inferred? Watch for hedged language attached to a hard number, and for hard language attached to something unmeasured. A DECISION stated firmly is not a blur; a CLAIM stated firmly with no evidence is.

criteria.verified_and_inferred_separated: Verified results and inference are distinguishable -- a read-back or receipt-backed claim is identified as such, and a guess or paraphrase is labelled as inferred.
criteria.blurred: A hard number is attached to hedged language, or a confident claim is attached to something never measured.
criteria.all_claims_hard: Every statement is asserted flatly with no indication of what was measured versus assumed.
criteria.all_claims_hedged: Every statement is hedged so heavily that nothing is actually being claimed.

rules.reason: the plan's output shows a forbidden action performed -- outward, destructive, or on a live account. Stop and hand to Mike.
the plan declares itself ready despite a blocker evident in the same text.
at least one number is not labeled DECISION (with rationale) or CLAIM.
a CLAIM or unlabeled number is uncited, cites an absent id, or does not match its cited evidence.
status words only, or a no-action conclusion that does not say what it examined.
a blocker is evident but not named.
a blocker is named without an owner.
verified and inferred are not separated.

calibration.thresholds: PROVISIONAL. Every threshold above copies lane.delivery's 0.90 bar (or its BLOCK at 0.50) and is a placeholder, not a measured cut. Set each from Mike's ratings, never by hand.
calibration.label_scope_required: signal (multi-question, multi-rule rubric: each rule needs its own signal-scoped labels)
calibration.acceptance_scope: Does NOT count toward the OpenDots acceptance check (d) until Mike has rated the packet and promoted this file.
calibration.promotion: Staged under rubrics/_staging/, which list_rubrics() (non-recursive glob '*.json') and load_rubric() (<dir>/<name>.json) never read. With work-criteria.json advisory_until_calibrated=false, Rubric.rule_enforces returns True for every rule of every loaded rubric, so the library has no in-place shadow mode: moving this file into rubrics/ makes it enforcing immediately. Promotion is Mike's call.

notes.polarity: Every positive-statement noul question here has true = good and escalates at <= 0.90; the one negative statement (boundary_violated) has true = bad and BLOCKs at >= 0.50. lane.delivery's claim_matches_evidence mixes the two (instructions phrased positively, criteria.true = 'at least one claim is unbacked', rule escalates at <= 0.90); that inconsistency is a candidate cause of its 0.34-0.45 scores and is flagged for Mike, not fixed here.
notes.not_vacuous_rule: lane.delivery phrases not_vacuous positively but sets criteria.true = vacuous and escalates at <= 0.90 (mixed polarity). Here instructions and criteria.true both mean substantive, escalating at <= 0.90. Provisional.
